message.content: {"caption":"Side-by-side schematic comparing a conventional memory store with an agentic memory that has direct links between the agent and stored items.","description":"Two workflow diagrams appear side by side. In (a), “Traditional memory system,” a blue-and-green globe icon labeled “Environment” connects to a blue robot icon labeled “LLM Agents”; the globe represents the agent’s environment and the robot represents the LLM agents. The “Interaction” connection has an arrow pointing from the Environment to the LLM Agents and another pointing back toward the Environment. The agents connect to “Memory,” depicted as three stacked lavender rectangular blocks: a right-pointing arrow labeled “Write” goes from the agents to the memory, and a left-pointing arrow labeled “Read” goes from the memory to the agents. In (b), “Our proposed agentic memory,” the Environment and LLM Agents have the same bidirectional Interaction connection. A right-pointing “Write” arrow and a left-pointing “Read” arrow connect the agents to the highlighted “Agentic Memory” region. Inside that region, a light-blue robot icon is linked to three stacked lavender memory blocks by three separate pairs of opposing arrows, showing connections in both directions; the blocks contain no visible text.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
